Title: Argument Injection in Decompression Reader via Malicious Filename
Analysis:
### Source
The untrusted input source is a user-controlled filename or filepath, which can be supplied as a command-line argument (e.g., via `--` to pass arguments starting with a hyphen) or can be present in a directory being searched (where wildcard expansion like `rg -z pattern -- *` passes it to `rg`).

### Sanitization/Validation
There is no sanitization or validation to check if the filename starts with a hyphen (`-`) or to prepend a `./` or use the `--` double-dash separator to signify the end of command options.

### Sink
The vulnerable sink is the invocation of `cmd.arg(path)` and the subsequent spawning of the decompression process inside `DecompressionReaderBuilder::build` in `crates/cli/src/decompress.rs`.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
If the user runs:
`rg -z "pattern" -- -someflag.gz`
The file `-someflag.gz` matches the `*.gz` glob, and `ripgrep` attempts to run `gzip -d -c -someflag.gz`.
Since `-someflag.gz` starts with a hyphen, `gzip` interprets it as a command-line option rather than a filename. Depending on the options supported by the decompression utilities (e.g., `gzip`, `xz`, `zstd`, `bzip2`, `lz4`), an attacker can cause unexpected command flags to be passed, leading to local file writes or other side effects depending on the underlying tool.

Title: Argument Injection in Preprocessor Execution via Malicious Filename
Analysis:
### Source
The untrusted input source is a user-controlled filename or filepath, which can be supplied as a command-line argument (e.g., via `--` to pass arguments starting with a hyphen) or can be present in a directory being searched (e.g. `rg --pre myprocessor pattern -- -someflag`).

### Sanitization/Validation
There is no sanitization or validation to check if the filename starts with a hyphen (`-`) or to prepend `./` or use the `--` double-dash separator to signify the end of command options.

### Sink
The vulnerable sink is the invocation of `cmd.arg(path)` and the subsequent spawning of the preprocessor process in `search_preprocessor` in `crates/core/search.rs`.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
If the user runs:
`rg --pre myprocessor "pattern" -- -someflag`
The file `-someflag` is passed as a positional argument. Under the hood, `ripgrep` attempts to run `myprocessor -someflag`.
Since `-someflag` starts with a hyphen, `myprocessor` interprets it as a command-line option rather than a filename. If the user-supplied preprocessor supports executing commands or modifying files via specific options (e.g., if `myprocessor` wraps tools like `find`, `awk`, or others), this leads to argument injection into the preprocessor, potentially allowing local arbitrary command execution.
